goal: Deliver the first executable Phase 2A coding-memory extraction slice, ingest three explicitly selected local Codex task histories as provenance-preserving events, and expose the resulting candidate-memory graph through a local 3D web inspection surface.
success_criteria: A bounded task-window ContextAssembler produces a deterministic input hash and evidence id set from immutable events.
A provider-replaceable extraction service validates strict ExtractionBatch output, persists idempotent extraction runs and candidate memories, and never mutates canonical events or stable cards.
Malformed or incomplete provider output is rejected with a durable run error and does not create unverifiable candidates.

The three user-authorized Codex task histories are converted from original message/file evidence into codememory.event.v1 records, ingested through IngestService, and retain thread, source, cwd, and completeness provenance.
A local HTTP graph endpoint and bundled 3D web page display tasks, sessions, evidence events, candidate memories, bindings, and evidence links from SQLite.
Existing Phase 0-1 tests remain green and new extraction, history-import, API, and UI smoke tests pass locally.
constraints: SQLite remains the canonical fact store; FTS, candidate search, and graph rows are rebuildable projections.
LLM and embedding providers are optional replaceable boundaries and are never on the synchronous event-ingest acknowledgement path.
Every candidate binding and relation must point to evidence event ids from the assembled input; hidden chain-of-thought is not persisted.
Only the three explicitly supplied Codex task ids may be used as real history input in this delivery.
Raw history archives containing local paths remain outside the repository; checked-in fixtures must be bounded and intentional.
The web page is a local inspection preview, not an authentication, cloud, or production deployment surface.
non_goals: Stable-card merge, supersede, stale, or forgetting lifecycle (Phase 3).
Code snapshot or symbol resolution against a live repository (Phase 4).
Embeddings, vector database, MCP adapter, Codex Desktop hook, or remote provider integration.
Production-grade 3D layout, collaboration, authentication, or hosted frontend.
stop_condition: Stop after the Phase 2A extraction, authorized history import, graph API/UI slice, regression checks, and artifact/verification ledger are complete; record Phase 3+ gaps instead of expanding scope.
